judged_text: The constructor now performs a blocking remote POST to login.salesforce.com and a Prisma credential.update on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where previously jsforce.Connection refreshed tokens lazily only when an access token expired. Every Salesforce calendar operation (and every booking touching Salesforce) now pays an extra OAuth round-trip plus a DB write per instantiation — a hot-path regression and a new network failure point that turns previously-cached-token operations into hard failures when Salesforce is slow or rate-limits.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new unconditional token refresh + DB write in `SalesforceCalendarService`: after `const credentialKey = credential.key...`, it immediately `fetch`es `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then runs `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no check for token expiry/need-to-refresh, so every service initialization now incurs a remote OAuth round-trip and a Prisma update, adding hot-path latency and a new failure point (e.g., slow/rate-limited Salesforce). This is a concrete performance/architecture regression risk rather than a strict correctness bug.
